NEUROLOGY NOTE   Date: 2026-04-14
25M, general wellness examination with neurology review.

S:
Patient presents for a wellness visit with attention to his neurologic status. He reports that his mobility has been stable but that leg fatigue limits how long he can stand and walk during a shift. He uses a walker for longer distances and manages well at home. He works part time as a library assistant reshelving materials. He could not complete 4 of his scheduled shifts last month because of symptoms. Sister with schizophrenia. Sleep is adequate and appetite is good. Lives with his parents, who assist with transportation. Never smoker, no alcohol.

O:
BP 116/72, HR 70, RR 14, Temp 98.3 F, SpO2 99% on room air. Weight 150 lb, BMI 22.
General: alert, pleasant, in no acute distress.
Neuro: spastic gait, uses a walker for distances, strength 4/5 in lower extremities, normal upper extremity tone, speech fluent.
CV: regular rate and rhythm, no murmur.
Lungs: clear to auscultation bilaterally.
Extremities: mild lower-limb spasticity, no contractures.
Labs (this week): basic metabolic panel within normal limits, CBC within normal limits.

A/P:
1. Cerebral palsy, ambulates with a walker. Continue physical therapy twice weekly and home stretching. Reassessed walker fit and referred to physiatry for a gait evaluation. Reviewed fall-prevention strategies at home and work and discussed botulinum toxin options for focal spasticity.
2. Health maintenance: reviewed age-appropriate preventive care and immunizations, which are up to date. Encouraged a seated strengthening routine between therapy sessions.
3. Function and work: current limits are affecting his ability to keep a full schedule. Provided a letter describing activity restrictions for his employer and recommended seated tasks where possible.

Return to clinic in 6 months, sooner if mobility changes or new concerns arise.
